title: Can Robotics Hackathon Change Your Life?
summary: The LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon brought thousands of participants together on June 14-15, 2025 for a 48-hour open-source robotics build sprint using Hugging Face’s LeRobot library. Projects ranged from t-shirt folding to Lego-sorting factories, and the event is framed as a concrete example of how accessible robot-learning tooling can pull beginners into hands-on AI robotics while seeding careers and research directions.

title: InOrbit.AI Demonstrates the Future of Multi-Vendor Robot Orchestration and Physical AI at Automate 2026
summary: InOrbit.AI used Automate 2026 to demonstrate multi-vendor robot orchestration, showing how robots from different suppliers can be coordinated through a shared operational layer rather than managed as isolated automation systems. The pitch is that Physical AI can turn fragmented fleets into a more unified and resilient “sentient enterprise,” where interoperability across vendors becomes central to scaling robotics in real-world operations.

extra.full_text: Experience the future of the sentient enterprise as InOrbit.AI orchestrates a groundbreaking multi-vendor robotics demonstration at Automate 2026. title: FORT Robotics extends its Trust Layer for Physical AI by adding Outside-In Safety in collaboration with NVIDIA Halos for Robotics
summary: FORT Robotics is extending its Trust Layer for Physical AI with Outside-In Safety, integrating external sensors alongside a robot’s onboard perception to monitor the surrounding environment and dynamically constrain or adjust robot behavior. Built in collaboration with NVIDIA Halos for Robotics, the approach aims to let robots operate closer to peak efficiency while maintaining safety through broader, site-level awareness rather than relying only on what the robot can sense locally.

extra.full_text: Extends robot perception beyond on-board sensors by including external sensors to dynamically control robot behavior and perform at maximum efficiency

title: Robot.com Launches R-noid, a Humanoid Built For the Work That Burns People Out. No Legs, All Lift to the Bottom Line.
summary: Robot.com launched R-noid, a legless humanoid platform aimed at repetitive industrial work that is hard to staff or burns out human workers. The company says it covers five solution categories and 19 deployable tasks, with a deployment path from initial site visit to autonomous operation in months, and plans to demonstrate it at Automate 2026.

title: Mantis Robotics Extends Potential of Physical AI with New Dual-Arm Fenceless Robot for Industrial and Retail Automation
summary: Mantis Robotics introduced the MR-X, a dual-arm fenceless robot for industrial and retail automation, at Automate 2026. It is positioned as a compact, high-speed system that can lift up to 70 lb without requiring safety cages, which could make dual-arm automation easier to deploy in space-constrained warehouses, factories, and retail backrooms.

extra.full_text: MR-X dual-arm robot debuts at Automate 2026 — Highest performing dual-arm robot lifting up to 70 lbs, with industrial speeds and compact footprint for deployment without cages.

title: Doosan Robotics Unveils AI Palletizing Solution PalletizHD+ at Automate 2026
summary: Doosan Robotics introduced PalletizHD+ at Automate 2026, an AI-enabled palletizing system that combines robotics with its PalletizOS software to help manufacturers raise throughput and reduce the complexity of palletizing operations. The company also showed AI-assisted sanding and welding systems using Physics-Informed AI and 3D vision, positioning its cobot lineup around more adaptive, perception-driven factory automation.

title: 美 GM, 디트로이트 '팩토리 제로' 공장에 협동로봇 50대 도입
summary: GM has added about 50 Fanuc collaborative robots to its Factory Zero EV plant in Detroit, where they work alongside remaining employees to attach body panels as vehicles move down the assembly line. The timing is politically charged because it follows layoffs of more than 1,000 workers at the same site amid slowing EV demand, making the deployment a flashpoint for union concerns about automation replacing labor despite GM’s safety and ergonomics framing.

extra.full_text: 제너럴모터스(GM)가 미국 미시간주 디트로이트에 있는 전기차 거점 공장 '팩토리 제로(Factory Zero)'에 협동로봇(cobot) 약 50대를 새로 도입했다고 미국 매체들이 보도했다. 이는 GM이 전기차 수요 둔화에 따라 같은 공장에서 1000명 이상의 인력을 감원한 직후 이뤄진 조치로, 노동조합의 반발을 사고 있다.새로 도입된 협동로봇은 일본 화낙(Fanuc)이 제작한 장비로, 차량이 조립 라인을 따라 이동하는 동안 남아 있는 작업자들과 함께 차체 패널을 부착하는 작업을 수행한다. title: NOVARC LAUNCHES NovAI AUTONOMY AS PART OF NovAI SUITE AND EXPANDS INTEGRATION TO YASKAWA AND ABB ROBOTS
summary: Novarc is adding NovAI Autonomy to its NovAI Suite, bringing machine vision and real-time adaptation into robotic welding so systems can adjust during the weld rather than just execute fixed paths. The launch also extends Novarc’s NovHub Enterprise Welding Intelligence platform to ABB and Yaskawa robots, making its monitoring and analytics stack available across more industrial welding cells.

extra.full_text: At the show, Novarc will unveil NovAI™ Autonomy, an advanced solution that brings machine vision and real-time adaptation to robotic welding; and NovHub™ - the company’s Enterprise Welding Intelligence platform - on ABB and Yaskawa robots.

title: Interview with Paul Dawalibi: Can Ras Al Khaimah become the Silicon Valley of the Middle East?
summary: Paul Dawalibi argues that Ras Al Khaimah is positioning itself as a smaller, more agile alternative to Dubai and Abu Dhabi for AI, robotics, and deep-tech companies entering the Middle East. The piece frames the emirate’s appeal around targeted investment and hub-building rather than sheer scale, suggesting that regional tech competition is widening beyond the UAE’s established centers.

extra.full_text: For decades, when technology companies looked to establish a presence in the Middle East, the conversation typically revolved around Dubai or Abu Dhabi. But as global competition for AI, robotics, and deep-tech investment intensifies, a growing number of smaller, more agile innovation hubs are seeking to carve out their own place in the technology landscape. title: From audio tapes to AI: Interview with TDK investment director Ankur Saxena
summary: TDK Ventures investment director Ankur Saxena argues that robotics investors may be overextending lessons from large language models and generative AI, treating robotics as if it will scale like software despite its hardware, sensing, and deployment constraints. The interview frames AI as the central investment theme but pushes for a more grounded view of robotics, where progress depends on embodied systems that can operate reliably in the physical world rather than on model capability alone.

title: KRISO, 수심 3500m급 심해 코어시추·환경감시 통합 무인체계 개발 착수
summary: KRISO has launched a government R&D project to build an integrated unmanned deep-sea exploration system by 2030, centered on a remotely operated vehicle for core drilling at depths of 3,500 meters and an autonomous underwater vehicle for monitoring environmental impacts. The effort brings together nine institutions, including RedOne Technology, Hanjin D&B, Seoul National University, and KAIST, and matters because it links resource sampling with in-situ environmental surveillance in the same deep-ocean operating concept.

title: 노타·오케스트로, 국토부 6109억 '천안·아산 AI 도시 구축 사업' 선정
summary: Cheonan and Asan were selected for South Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport AI-specialized pilot city program, a five-year project worth about 610.9 billion won through 2030. The 11-member consortium, including Upstage, Nota, Okestro, Ditonic, Clobot, KEPCO KDN, and KAIST’s Mobility AX Research Institute, will build an integrated urban intelligence center and test autonomous AI agent services for disaster response, traffic, and civil complaints.
